p:cNvPr.descr: An illustrated diagram showing the process of TAP tagging. The diagram begins with two separate images at the top. On the left is a target protein, represented by a red sphere, bound to the right to a TAP tag, which consists of a purple cylinder, bonded to a thinner cylinder, bound to a purple sphere named “protein A.” The purple cylinder is labeled “calmodulin-binding peptide” below and the smaller purple cylinder is labeled “TEV protease cleavage site.” The purple region is bracketed and labeled above “TAP tag.” The image to the right shows an image of assorted colored spheres in varying sizes. There are small gray proteins, larger white proteins, larger green proteins, and smaller orange proteins. A label at the top, pointing down to the green and orange proteins, reads, “Crude cell extract containing proteins that interact with target protein.” Two arrows come from these diagrams and merge into a single down arrow. To the right is a gray text box reading, “Run cell extract over first IgG affinity column, which binds protein A tag.” Below this arrow is the tagged target protein bonded left to 3 orange proteins and 3 green ones, surrounded by the gray and white proteins. On the right, protein A has bonded right to a large tan sphere with Y-shaped structures on it; this is labeled “IgG beads” to the right. Below is a down arrow with a divergent down arrow showing the exit of the gray and white proteins. To the right is a text box reading, “Proteins that do not interact with the target elute.” Below this is another down arrow with a text box on the right reading, “Cleave protein A with TEV protease.” Below this is an image of the TAP tagged target protein bonded right to the IgG beads, being attacked by an oval blue protein which is the TEV protease. It has a roughly triangular opening for an active site. Below this, a down arrow has a divergent arrow showing the removal of the target protein, which is red, attached to the green and orange proteins. Target protein elutes. Run eluate over calmodulin affinity column. Below, the small green and orange proteins in the surface of the target protein have begun to fall off; the orange ones scatter to the left of the target while the green proteins remain on. The target is still bonded right to the IgG by the calmodulin binding peptide. The IgG has lost its Y-shaped extensions. This is labeled “calmodulin beads” at right. Below is a down arrow with a divergent arrow showing the removal of the orange proteins. A text box to the right reads, “Loosely bound proteins elute.” Below, there is a second down arrow with a text box to the right reading, “Elute target protein with excess calmodulin.” Below is the final protein, which is the red target bonded right to the purple calmodulin-binding peptide; the red target is covered in green proteins. This is labeled right, “Eluted protein complexes.”

p:cNvPr.descr: A diagram showing process of using epitope tags to study interactions between proteins. The diagram begins with a strand of DNA containing a short blue section at the left end, followed by an orange region labeled “promoter”. To the right is a yellow section labeled “cDNA”, a red section labeled “epitope tag”, and a plain short blue section. The word “transcription” appears above with a right arrow. To the right there is a down and right curved arrow pointing to a gray cell. The cell has a darker gray nucleus with a blue mass of genetic material inside. A small amount of the genetic material is red and orange. To the right inside the cell are a few orange and yellow proteins. To the left is a gray text box reading, “Express tagged protein in a cell.” Below is a left and down curved arrow with a gray text box labeled “make cell extract.” The arrow points to an illustration of a test tube filled with a light blue liquid with orange dots floating in it. Many of these have sunk toward the bottom and built up there. This is labeled “immunoprecipitate” below. To the left is a gray text box reading, “Precipitate tagged protein with speciﬁc antibody.” Below there is a down and left arrow pointing to a gray text box reading, “Separate precipitated proteins.” Below this is an image of several bands showing the presence of different proteins. The bands are on a pale blue square and separated into three columns. The leftmost column is labeled “size markers” with a long line of bands of similar thickness and color but different color saturations. Some are very dark bands and others are light. The column to the right is labeled “pure tagged protein”, under which there is only a single band, medium purple and aligning with the third size marker down. To the right, the third column is labeled “immunoprecipitate” and has four bands beneath, at size markers 1, 3, 4, and 6. To the right is an arrow pointing to a text box reading, “Identify new proteins in immunoprecipitate.”
